plugins.name: design-review
plugins.description: Expert design and UX review of rendered web apps, websites, app UI flows, infographics, and design artifacts — the last pass before a human looks at AI-built UI. Runs deterministic accessibility, performance, contrast, motion and layout-integrity gates, then structural, state, component-inventory, craft, flow and design-system passes against real renders at multiple viewports, and returns severity-ranked findings with pasteable fixes and evidence. Use this whenever someone asks to review, audit, critique, QA, sanity-check or "give feedback on" a UI, page, screen, flow, prototype, landing page, dashboard, deck or design — or says their UI "looks AI-generated", "looks off", "feels cheap", "needs polish", "isn't accessible", or asks whether something is ready to ship or ready for a human to look at. Also use it before shipping any UI that Claude or another AI tool generated, even when nobody used the word "review". v1.2.0 hardens against the two silent coverage failures: a review covering a subset of surfaces, and a review writing the report after only some pipeline stages. Both previously produced a report formally indistinguishable from a finished one. The surface set and the stage set are now enumerations fixed at stage 0, held in a scripts/worklist.py ledger (init fixes the count, set marks cells done or n/a-with-reason, check exits non-zero while any cell is open) so 'the review is finished' is an exit code rather than a feeling; an unrecognised cell counts as open deliberately. run_review.py gains --worklist/--surface and marks only the gates and render cells a successful capture actually proves. The surface sweep is the one loop with no budget, because a budget on it is indistinguishable from an excuse; the whole-review exit now also requires no open ledger cell. The verdict line carries the surface fraction on complete reviews too, so its absence never marks a review finished, and the coverage denominator comes from the stage-0 worklist rather than from what got reviewed. Stopping short is declared with a resume point; sampling is legitimate when declared with its basis and stated blind spots, silent sampling is not. Also adds imitation material as a craft finding and two Tier 2 source rules for it (stacked-inset-bevel, letterpress-text-shadow) with an evals fixture that drives both, a rebuild escalation when fixing every listed finding still would not produce a passable surface, and a rule that a fix invisible in the recapture is unresolved however confident the edit felt.
